title: Online Safety Amendment (Protecting Australian Children from Online Harm) Bill 2023
short_title: Online Safety Amendment (Protecting Australian Children from Online Harm) Bill 2023

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require the federal minister for online safety to run a test of tools that check how old a user is.
The test would follow a plan the eSafety Commissioner published in August 2023 for stopping children from seeing harmful material online.
The government had earlier rejected the idea of a test and instead wanted industry rules, but the Coalition supports the trial this bill would start.
changes: Requires the minister to conduct an age verification trial.
Aligns the trial with the eSafety Commissioner's August 2023 Roadmap.
Responds to a referral from the former Coalition Government after the 2020 Protecting the Age of Innocence report.
summary.affected: The minister, the eSafety Commissioner, and children who might be protected from online harms such as pornography.
